newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rundle shale twins to raise A$90 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rundle shale twins to raise A$90 mln.

text.p: The two companies developing the Stuart shale oil project in Queensland, known as the Rundle twins, said on Wednesday they had acceptances from institutional investors for share issues raising a total of A$89.95 million.

Southern Pacific Petroleum NL would issue 10.8 million shares at A$4.15 a share to raise A$44.82 million while Central Pacific Minerals NL would issue 4.75 million shares at A$9.50 a share to raise A$45.13 million, they said.

Southern Pacific and Central Pacific said they had initially looked at an offering through brokers Wilson HTM and SBC Warburg to raise A$80 million, but had found acceptances substantially exceeded this amount.
"Completion of the placement will finalise SPP/CPM funding requirements and enable the sponsors to proceed with construction of Stuart Stage 1," they said in a statement.
The companies announced earlier this month they had agreed with financiers and the Queensland government to proceed with stage one of the Stuart shale oil project.
The Stuart Shale project is being developed jointly between the Rundle Twins and Canada's Suncor Inc.

Stuart stage one is the first of three planned stages to develop the oil shale deposit and involves construction of a plant to produce 4,500 barrels of oil per day at an estimated cost of A$250 million.
The companies said subsequent stages could raise production progressively to a total of 95,000 barrels per day with the prospect of additional production thereafter.
Southern Pacific's shares closed down 21 cents at A$4.30 on Wednesday, while Central Pacific's shares closed 40 cents higher at A$10.50.
Central Pacific and Southern Pacific are also listed in the United States.
